Trying to get a reproducible case -- strangely enough it appears to always happen on split packets, after reading the first 57 bytes of the split packet -- no idea where 57 comes from.
My guess is that the fix doesn't handle the case where the buffer contains multiple TLS records whose last record is truncated.  I didn't have a chance to confirm this by myself though.

Maybe I can check this in a few.. Just time for dinner first

Am 07.07.2013 um 18:39 schrieb Trustin Lee notifications@github.com:

> My guess is that the fix doesn't handle the case where the buffer contains multiple TLS records whose last record is truncated. I didn't have a chance to confirm this by myself though.
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub.

In each case, the first packet contained a 32-byte TLS record (not including header) and then the first 314-bytes of the second TLS record (also not including header) -- so the first packet was 356 bytes total. Then the second packet consumed the first 57 bytes and the next time through caused the exception.

Not necessarily related but looks like another bug: `decode0()` calls `ctx.fireMessageReceived()` where `out.add(...)` should be called.  i.e. we should not extend ByteToMessageDecoder really.

I'll take a closer look in the morning.

Hmm... We used FrameDecoder in 3.x so I think it should be ok to use ByteToMessageDecoder in 4.x

Am 07.07.2013 um 18:59 schrieb Jeff Pinner notifications@github.com:

> @trustin, just took a look at your fix, you're right -- you shouldn't just reset packetLength to 0 in the finally block, you need to add:
> 
> packetLength -= result.bytesConsumed()
> 
> after the unwrap call and read the next header once it reaches 0.
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub.
@trustin now I see.. I think you are right we should better not extend ByteToMessageDecoder at all and just handle it by ourself.
@normanmaurer In Netty 3.x we skipped the decoded packet length and returned the unwrapped buffer. So we never processed more than 1 frame at a time.
@trustin how did you generate your ssl test data ? just capture it via wireshark ?
